lines: That thought came in muddy and left tracks.
I have seen trampled crops with more sense than that.
Careful. Even soil looks softer than your manners right now.
I have seen broken crops with better instincts than you.
You have the manners of a boot in fresh soil.
I have pulled weeds with better intentions.
That idea should have stayed buried.
You are as helpful as rain through a broken roof.
Even a scarecrow knows when to stand still and be useful.
Your confidence grows faster than your sense, which is saying something.
I would not feed that opinion to compost.
You trample a mood like wheat under heavy feet.
A crooked fence offers better support than you just did.
You are proof that not everything grows from good seed.
That remark was all husk and no grain.
The field has seen worse weather and still complained less.
You make mud look thoughtful.
A dry well has more to offer than that.
Your sense needs weeding and a long season.
Mud carries itself with more dignity than you do.
I would not plant that opinion in poor soil.
Your manners could sour a full barrel of apples.
I asked for sense, not noise with boots on.
Leave the fields out of whatever foolishness you brought here.
Wipe your feet before you bring the whole road inside.
If you want respect, begin by showing some.
Do not touch what you did not help make.
You have a remarkable gift for arriving at the wrong moment.
Speak plainly. I am not sorting through your attitude too.
The village has chores for people with that much spare energy.
Keep your hands to yourself and your excuses shorter.
I heard you the first time. Repeating it did not improve it.
You can leave before your manners get any worse.
Try asking like the answer belongs to another person.
I have work that deserves more attention than this.
Being loud does not make you right.
If that was meant to impress me, it missed.
You are testing patience you did not earn.
Come back when you can manage a civil sentence.
I will not clean up another mess made by your pride.
